article.title: Why ‘Up 10%’ Does Not Always Mean ‘10 Percentage Points’
article.why: Learn the difference between percent change and percentage-point change.

paragraphs.en:
People often use percent and percentage points as if they mean the same thing. They do not. The difference is especially important when we talk about conversion rates, survey results, market share, or experiment results.

Imagine that a website’s conversion rate rises from 10 percent to 12 percent. The direct difference is 2 percentage points: 12 minus 10 equals 2. But the percent increase is 20 percent, because the rate increased by 2 compared with the original value of 10.

Now imagine another rate rises from 50 percent to 52 percent. This is also an increase of 2 percentage points, but the relative increase is only 4 percent. The same percentage-point change can therefore represent a very different percent change depending on the starting value.

This distinction matters in business reports. If an A/B test raises conversion from 1 percent to 1.2 percent, saying ‘conversion increased by 0.2 percent’ can confuse readers. The absolute change is 0.2 percentage points, while the relative increase is 20 percent. Both statements can be useful, but they answer different questions.

A simple rule helps. Use percentage points when you subtract one percentage rate from another. Use percent when you describe the change relative to the original value. If possible, report both: ‘Conversion increased from 1.0% to 1.2%, an increase of 0.2 percentage points or 20% relative.’

Clear wording prevents small numbers from sounding misleadingly large or important changes from sounding too small. Before saying a metric is ‘up 10%,’ check whether you really mean percent or percentage points.
paragraphs.zh:
人們常把 percent 與 percentage points 當成同一件事，但兩者不同，尤其在 conversion rate、問卷比例、市占率或實驗結果中非常重要。

例如網站轉換率從10%升到12%，直接差值是2個百分點；但相對於原本10%，增幅其實是20%。若另一個比例從50%升到52%，同樣增加2個百分點，但相對增幅只有4%。

因此同樣的 percentage-point change，依起始值不同可能代表完全不同的 percent change。A/B test 若從1%升到1.2%，absolute change 是0.2 percentage points，relative increase 則是20%。兩種說法都有意義，但回答不同問題。

簡單規則是：兩個百分比直接相減時用 percentage points；相對原始值描述增減幅時用 percent。最好同時報告，例如「Conversion 從1.0%升至1.2%，增加0.2個百分點，相對增幅20%。」

清楚區分可以避免小數字被說得過大，也避免重要變化看起來太小。說「up 10%」之前，先確認你真正指的是 percent 還是 percentage points。
paragraphs.ja:
percentとpercentage pointは同じ意味ではありません。conversion rate、構成比、市場share、A/B testの結果では特に重要です。

例えばconversion rateが10％から12％になった場合、直接の差は2 percentage pointsです。一方、元の10％に対する相対増加率は20％です。50％から52％の場合も2 points増ですが、相対増加率は4％にすぎません。

つまり同じpercentage-point changeでもstarting valueによってpercent changeは異なります。A/B testで1％から1.2％になった場合、absolute changeは0.2 points、relative increaseは20％です。どちらも有用ですが、別の問いに答えています。

簡単なruleとして、二つの率を引き算した差にはpercentage pointsを使い、元の値に対する変化率にはpercentを使います。可能なら「1.0％から1.2％へ上昇し、0.2ポイント増、相対的には20％増」のように両方示すと明確です。

表現を区別すれば、小さな数字を過大に見せたり、重要な変化を小さく見せたりする誤解を防げます。

vocabulary.usage: The rate rose by two percentage points.
The starting value affects relative change.

business.term: Conversion increased by 0.2 percentage points, or 20% relative to baseline.
business.explanation: 同時報告絕對百分點差與相對增幅。
